title: Increase payroll tax rate to 16.0 percent in 2025 and later
description: Increase the payroll tax rate (currently 12.4 percent) to 16.0 percent in 2025 and later.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 3.51% of payroll; 75th year effect: 3.62% of payroll

title: Increase payroll tax rate to 15.9 percent in 2035-2064, and to 19.4 percent in years 2065 and later
description: Increase the payroll tax rate (currently 12.4 percent) to 15.9 percent in 2035-2064, and to 19.4 percent in years 2065 and later.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 4.13% of payroll; 75th year effect: 6.95% of payroll

title: Increase payroll tax rate by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2030-2049
description: Increase the payroll tax rate (currently 12.4 percent) by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2030-2049, until the rate reaches 14.4 percent in 2049 and later.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 1.50% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.02% of payroll

title: Increase payroll tax rate by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2027-2032
description: Increase the payroll tax rate (currently 12.4 percent) by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2027-2032, until the rate reaches 13.0 percent for 2032 and later.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 0.55% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.61% of payroll

title: Increase payroll tax rate by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2028-2051
description: Increase the payroll tax rate (currently 12.4 percent) by 0.1 percentage point each year from 2028-2051, until the rate reaches 14.8 percent in 2051 and later.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 1.79% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.42% of payroll

title: Increase payroll tax rate by 0.1 percentage point per year for 2026 through 2035
description: Increase the payroll tax rate by 0.1 percentage point per year for 2026 through 2035 so that it equals 13.4 percent for 2035 and later. The increase would be split evenly between the employer and employee share, and would be split between OASI and DI in proportion to currently scheduled payroll tax rates.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes; Broadens funding base; Long-range effect: 0.90% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.01% of payroll

title: Eliminate the taxable maximum with benefit credit
description: Eliminate the taxable maximum in years 2025 and later, and apply full 12.4 percent payroll tax rate to all earnings. Provide benefit credit for earnings above the current-law taxable maximum.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes while maintaining benefit fairness; Long-range effect: 1.86% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.37% of payroll

title: Phase in elimination of taxable maximum with secondary PIA formula
description: Eliminate the taxable maximum for years 2031 and later (phased in 2025-2031), and apply full 12.4 percent payroll tax rate to all earnings. Provide benefit credit for earnings above the current-law taxable maximum that are subject to the payroll tax, using a secondary PIA formula.
impacts: Increases revenue through payroll tax changes with progressive benefit structure; Long-range effect: 2.37% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.49% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $250,000
description: Apply 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $250,000 starting in 2025, and tax all earnings once the current-law taxable maximum exceeds $250,000. Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Increases revenue by targeting very high earners; Creates a donut hole approach; Long-range effect: 2.49% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.60% of payroll

title: Phase in elimination of taxable maximum with 5% formula factor
description: Eliminate the taxable maximum in years 2030 and later. Phase in elimination by taxing all earnings above the current-law taxable maximum at increasing rates. Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with a 5 percent formula factor.
impacts: Increases revenue with incremental implementation; Long-range effect: 2.22% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.20% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $400,000
description: Apply 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $400,000 starting in 2025 and tax all earnings once the current-law taxable maximum exceeds $400,000. Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Increases revenue by targeting very high earners; Long-range effect: 2.01% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.15% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $400,000 with benefit credit
description: Apply OASDI 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $400,000 starting in 2026, and tax all earnings once the current-law taxable maximum exceeds $400,000. Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with 2 percent formula factor.
impacts: Increases revenue while providing some benefit credit for additional taxes; Long-range effect: 2.20% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.45% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $250,000 with benefit credit
description: Apply OASDI 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $250,000 starting in 2026. Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with 2 percent formula factor.
impacts: Increases revenue by targeting high earners with some benefit credit; Long-range effect: 2.38% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.44% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $300,000 with benefit credit
description: Apply OASDI 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $300,000 starting in 2026. Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with 3 percent formula factor.
impacts: Increases revenue with higher benefit credit percentage for affected earnings; Long-range effect: 2.28% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.36% of payroll

title: Apply 12.4% payroll tax on earnings above $250,000 with wage index adjustment
description: Apply OASDI 12.4 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $250,000 starting in 2025. Increase the computed level of the SSA average wage index for years after 2024. Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula.
impacts: Complex approach with both tax changes and wage index adjustments; Long-range effect: 2.34% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.38% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% of earnings
description: Increase the taxable maximum such that 90 percent of earnings would be subject to the payroll tax (phased in 2025-2034). Provide benefit credit for earnings up to the revised taxable maximum.
impacts: Increases taxable earnings base more broadly; Long-range effect: 2.18% of payroll; 75th year effect: 2.46% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% without benefit credit
description: Increase the taxable maximum such that 90 percent of earnings would be subject to the payroll tax (phased in 2025-2034). Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Increases revenue without increasing benefits; Long-range effect: 0.84% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.69% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% with benefit credit
description: Increase the taxable maximum such that 90 percent of earnings would be subject to the payroll tax (phased in 2025-2034). Provide benefit credit for earnings up to the revised taxable maximum.
impacts: Increases revenue with proportional benefit increases; Long-range effect: 1.08% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.19% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum by 2% per year starting in 2025
description: Increase the taxable maximum each year by an additional 2 percent beginning in 2025 until taxable earnings equal 90 percent of covered earnings. Provide benefit credit for earnings up to the revised taxable maximum.
impacts: Gradual increase in taxable earnings base; Long-range effect: 0.70% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.72% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum by 2% per year starting in 2027 without benefit credit
description: Increase the taxable maximum each year by an additional 2 percent beginning in 2027 until taxable earnings equal 90 percent of covered earnings. Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Increases revenue without increasing benefits; Long-range effect: 0.83% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.19% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum by 2% per year with 5% formula factor
description: Increase the taxable maximum by an additional 2 percent per year beginning in 2026 until taxable earnings equal 90 percent of covered earnings. Provide benefit credit with a 5 percent formula factor applying above the current-law taxable maximum.
impacts: Progressive approach with greater revenue gains than benefit increases; Long-range effect: 0.72% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.87% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings over $366,000 with proportional credit
description: Beginning in 2032, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate on earnings over the wage-indexed equivalent of $200,000 in 2017 (about $366,000 in 2032), with proportional benefit credit.
impacts: Modest additional revenue with proportional benefits; Long-range effect: 0.18% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.10% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings over $366,000 without benefit credit
description: Beginning in 2032, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate on earnings over the wage-indexed equivalent of $200,000 in 2017 (about $366,000 in 2032). Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Targets high earners with no additional benefits; Long-range effect: 0.26% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.30% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings over $549,000 with proportional credit
description: Beginning in 2032, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate on earnings over the wage-indexed equivalent of $300,000 in 2017 (about $549,000 in 2032), with proportional benefit credit.
impacts: Very targeted approach for highest earners; Long-range effect: 0.13% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.07% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings over $549,000 without benefit credit
description: Beginning in 2032, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate on earnings over the wage-indexed equivalent of $300,000 in 2017 (about $549,000 in 2032). Do not provide benefit credit for additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Increased revenue from highest earners; Long-range effect: 0.19% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.22% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum by twice the rate of AWI but never below 3%
description: Beginning in 2026, increase the taxable maximum by twice the rate of increase in the national Average Wage Index, but never by less than 3 percent. Provide benefit credit for earnings up to the revised taxable maximum levels.
impacts: Accelerated growth in taxable maximum with minimum increase guarantee; Long-range effect: 0.16% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.18% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% plus 6.2% tax rate above that level
description: Increase the taxable maximum such that 90 percent of earnings are subject to the payroll tax (phased in 2025-2034). In addition, apply a tax rate of 6.2 percent for earnings above the revised taxable maximum. Provide benefit credit for earnings taxed up to the revised taxable maximum.
impacts: Two-tier approach with significant revenue increase; Long-range effect: 1.56% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.45% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to $291,000 by 2029
description: Increase the taxable maximum linearly over 4 years to $291,000 for 2029. After 2029, index the taxable maximum to AWI plus 0.5 percentage point. Apply benefit credit on additional earnings taxed.
impacts: Specific target increase with higher indexing; Long-range effect: 1.52% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.41% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% with new bend point
description: Increase the taxable maximum by an additional 2 percent per year beginning in 2026 until taxable earnings equal 90 percent of covered earnings. Create a new bend point equal to the current-law taxable maximum with a 5 percent formula factor applying above the new bend point.
impacts: Combination of tax base increase and benefit formula change; Long-range effect: 0.32% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.33% of payroll

title: Increase taxable maximum to 90% with 2.5% formula factor
description: Increase the taxable maximum such that 90 percent of earnings would be subject to the payroll tax (phased in linearly from 2026-2031). Provide benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with a 2.5 percent formula factor.
impacts: Progressive approach with targeted benefit increases; Long-range effect: 1.13% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.56% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings over $500,000
description: Beginning in 2026, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate for earnings above the wage-indexed equivalent of $400,000 in 2017 (about $500,000 in 2026), with proportional benefit credit using a PIA formula factor of 0.5 percent.
impacts: Moderate additional revenue from very high earners; Long-range effect: 0.66% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.72% of payroll

title: Apply 2% payroll tax rate on earnings above $400,000 (not indexed)
description: Beginning in 2026, apply 2 percent payroll tax rate on earnings above $400,000 (not indexed for future years). Provide proportional benefit credit using a secondary PIA formula with a 0.5 percent formula factor.
impacts: Targets high earners with threshold that captures more income over time; Long-range effect: 1.05% of payroll; 75th year effect: 1.11% of payroll
